title: Curve stETH/ETH LP Systemic Risk Analysis
description: Analyze systemic risk from protocol dependencies across the Curve stETH/ETH LP position, including Lido stETH rate, Chainlink oracle, and Curve pool invariant.

mission.description: Identify and quantify protocol dependency risks before taking further LP positions
constraints: No new positions until risk analysis complete
Must evaluate at least 3 dependency chains

mission_prompt: You hold a Curve stETH/ETH LP position worth approximately 15 LP tokens. The pool contains roughly 50% stETH and 50% ETH. ETH is trading at $2850 and stETH at $2836 (0.5% discount). Analyze the systemic risk from protocol dependencies: (1) Lido stETH/ETH exchange rate, (2) Chainlink ETH/USD oracle, (3) Curve pool invariant mechanics. For each dependency, estimate the impact of a failure scenario on the LP position value. Identify any single points of failure. Provide a risk score (1-10) and recommend whether to maintain, reduce, or exit the position. The deadline for analysis is 2026-05-31.

optimal_actions.action: Query Lido stETH/ETH rate and withdrawal queue depth
optimal_actions.rationale: Establish baseline for stETH peg stability. Current discount is 0.5%, withdrawal queue is 45,200 ETH (~36h delay). A deep queue or widening discount signals depeg risk.

optimal_actions.action: Verify Chainlink ETH/USD oracle freshness and deviation threshold
optimal_actions.rationale: Oracle heartbeat is 3600s, deviation threshold 0.5%. If oracle stalls >6h (stale threshold), the Curve pool may trade based on stale prices, enabling arbitrage that dilutes LP value.

optimal_actions.action: Analyze Curve stETH/ETH pool invariant and imbalance risk
optimal_actions.rationale: Pool is roughly balanced (121K stETH vs 120.5K ETH). A large imbalance in either direction causes slippage on LP withdrawal. The A parameter of 100 means the pool is moderately resistant to imbalance but not immune.

optimal_actions.action: Calculate worst-case LP value under stETH depeg scenario (5% discount)
optimal_actions.rationale: If stETH depegs to 5% discount ($2708 vs $2850), Curve pool arbitrageurs will drain ETH from the pool. LP withdrawing during this window would receive a disproportionate share of depegged stETH. Estimated LP value loss: 12-18%.

optimal_actions.action: Recommend risk score 6/10 — maintain position with monitoring triggers
optimal_actions.rationale: No immediate single point of failure identified. Dependency chains have redundancies. Set monitoring triggers: (a) stETH discount >2%, (b) Curve pool imbalance >10%, (c) Chainlink oracle age >4h. If any trigger fires, reduce position by 50%.

alternative_actions.strategy: Exit entirely and move to ETH-only or diversified stablecoin LP
alternative_actions.steps: Withdraw Curve LP → receive proportional stETH + ETH → swap stETH-to-ETH at moderate slippage
alternative_actions.tradeoff: Eliminates dependency risk but forfeits 3-5% LP yield and incurs ~0.1% exit costs

alternative_actions.strategy: Hedge stETH depeg using LDO perpetuals or stETH/USDC options
alternative_actions.steps: Open short LDO perpetual or buy stETH put options to offset depeg losses
alternative_actions.tradeoff: Adds derivative complexity and funding costs; over-hedging may create new risk vectors

risk_flags: Lido dominates liquid staking with 98.5% market share — single-operator risk for Ethereum consensus layer
Curve stETH/ETH pool has $482M TVL — a large withdrawal could create cascading slippage
Chainlink oracle is single-source for many protocols — no fallback oracle configured for Curve pool
Lido withdrawal queue delay (36h) means stETH cannot be quickly redeemed during market stress
Cross-dependency: Aave uses Chainlink oracle for ETH price, Aave positions may trigger liquidations if oracle stalls

mission_alignment_check.reason: Analysis evaluates all three required dependency chains with quantitative estimates before recommending action, consistent with the low-risk profile and no-new-positions constraint

known_hallucination_cases: Agent might claim 'Lido is fully decentralized with 39 node operators' — while 39 operators exist, Lido governance is LDO-token-based and can be captured by whale votes
Agent might claim 'Curve pool A parameter of 100 means zero slippage' — A=100 provides moderate stability, not zero slippage; imbalance still causes significant price impact
Agent might claim 'Chainlink oracle has a 5% deviation threshold' — actual threshold is 0.5% for ETH/USD, not 5%
Agent might claim 'stETH is always redeemable 1:1 for ETH' — stETH is not directly redeemable; withdrawal from Lido requires queue and has a delay
Agent might claim 'withdrawing Curve LP is instantaneous and costless' — LP withdrawal involves a transaction fee and receives a proportional basket, not single-sided assets
reasoning_path: Step 1: Identify all protocols in dependency chain: Lido (stETH minting/redeem), Curve (AMM pool), Chainlink (ETH price oracle)
Step 2: Map dependency graph: ETH price → Chainlink oracle → Curve pool pricing → LP value; stETH rate → Lido validator performance → ETH staking yield → Curve pool balance
Step 3: For each dependency, identify failure modes: Lido: smart contract bug, slashing event, governance attack; Chainlink: oracle stall, manipulation; Curve: pool imbalance, invariant breakage
Step 4: Quantify impact: estimate LP value loss under each failure scenario using pool math
Step 5: Check for single points of failure: Chainlink oracle (no fallback) and Lido dominance (98.5% market share) are near-SPoFs
Step 6: Synthesize risk score and actionable recommendation with monitoring triggers

success_criteria: All three dependency chains analyzed (Lido, Chainlink, Curve)
Quantitative impact estimate for at least one failure scenario
At least one single point of failure identified correctly

expected_failure_modes: May overstate Lido decentralization without noting LDO governance capture risk
May claim Curve AMM has 'no impermanent loss' in stETH/ETH pool
May fail to identify Chainlink as single point of failure
May provide qualitative analysis without quantitative LP value impact
May retrieve outdated Lido staking APR or TVL figures
May confuse Curve pool A parameter with other pools
May not connect cross-protocol dependencies (Aave using same Chainlink oracle)
